headline: GOLD DROPS TO $4,017 AS IRAN SHUTS HORMUZ — Oil Shock Raises Inflation Fears, Kills Safe-Haven Bid; Miners Slide With Metals
snippet: Gold fell to $4,017 Wednesday — down 2.63% to its lowest since July 1 — in a counterintuitive reversal of the traditional safe-haven playbook: Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz is driving oil prices sharply higher, raising U.S. inflation expectations and keeping the Federal Reserve hawkish, which strengthens the dollar and weighs on non-yielding gold. Silver slipped to $58.26, also off roughly 2.4%. Markets are now explicitly pricing 'Hormuz = hawkish Fed' rather than 'Hormuz = safe-haven bid' — the precise dynamic that punishes mining stocks even as a shooting war unfolds in the Gulf.

headline: RARE EARTH CLEAN SWEEP: ALL 18 ELEMENTS UP IN JULY — Germanium +27.8%, Dysprosium +25.4%, Indium +26.5%; First Broad-Based Advance of 2026
snippet: Every one of the 18 rare earth elements tracked by market monitors rose in July 2026 — the first genuinely broad-based advance of the year, compared to the sharp, narrow moves that defined H1. Germanium led with +27.8%, dysprosium reversed with +25.4% to $261.63/kg (its largest single-month move this year), and indium gained 26.5%, with the basket averaging 16.7% gains and zero declines. U.S. rare earth stocks had already surged 81% in H1 before pulling back since June 30; this month's price-level advances lay fresh fundamental support beneath the sector.

headline: ADAM HAMILTON: GDX TOP 25 HEADING FOR NEAR-RECORD Q2 — $2,787/oz Implied Profit, +50% YoY; Sector P/E Collapsed From 49x to 20x Since 2023
snippet: Adam Hamilton's latest GoldSeek analysis frames the upcoming Q2 2026 earnings season as gold miners' second-best quarter ever: with Q2 average gold near $4,512 and assumed all-in sustaining costs of $1,725/oz, implied unit profits reach $2,787/oz — a 50% year-over-year jump from Q2 2025's $1,861/oz and second only to Q1 2026's record $3,129/oz. Over the last twelve consecutive quarters, GDX top-25 implied profits have compounded year-over-year between 31% and 113%; yet the sector's trailing price/earnings ratio has collapsed from 49.6x in Q4 2023 to just 20.2x following Q1 2026 results — one of the sharpest valuation disconnects in the current mining cycle.

headline: US$372M MEXICO GOLD MERGER CLOSES FRIDAY — Goldgroup Wins Final Court Order; Multi-Mine Sonora + Oaxaca + Michigan Producer Eyes NYSE American (GORO / GGAZF)
snippet: Goldgroup Mining received BC Supreme Court's final order for its combination with Gold Resource Corporation (NYSE American: GORO), setting July 17 as the expected closing date for the US$372 million deal that creates a Mexico-focused multi-mine precious metals producer — Cerro Prieto mine and San Francisco project in Sonora, Don David mine in Oaxaca, and Back Forty project in Michigan. Both companies' shareholders approved the deal July 2 with 99.99% support; Goldgroup implements a 4:1 share consolidation to meet NYSE American price thresholds. Gold Resource shareholders retain approximately 40% of the combined entity.

headline: SIERRA MADRE WINS SEMARNAT GREEN LIGHT — 22 Drill Pads Approved at Guitarra Silver-Gold East District; Phase 1 of 30,000m Program Commencing Within 60 Days (TSXV: SM)
source_name: INN / Sierra Madre Gold and Silver
snippet: Sierra Madre Gold and Silver Ltd. (TSXV: SM) received SEMARNAT approval July 14 for 22 drill pads at the East District of its Guitarra silver-gold complex in Guerrero State, Mexico — the first phase of a fully budgeted 30,000-metre drill program that will test up to 30 mapped vein systems never previously drilled. The Guitarra Mine is a permitted underground operation with a 500 tpd processing facility that restarted commercial production in January 2025; the East District represents high-priority exploration upside beyond the existing permitted footprint, with contractor bids now being received and drilling expected to commence within 60 days.

headline: PROSPECT RIDGE DRILLS VIRGIN EXCALIBUR PORPHYRY — Babine Belt's Largest Undrilled Cu-Au Target Gets First Diamond Core; 1,500m Program Launched (CSE: PRR)
snippet: Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. (CSE: PRR) began drilling July 12 at its 100%-owned Excalibur copper-gold porphyry project in BC's Babine district — the same belt as former producers Huckleberry, Bell, and Granisle mines. The inaugural program targets an undrilled 2 km² soil-covered anomaly where a completed induced polarization survey revealed a large chargeability feature interpreted as a pyrite-bearing halo flanking magnetite-rich potassic alteration — the textbook porphyry fingerprint. Three to four planned holes totalling approximately 1,500 metres are underway, fully funded and permitted.

headline: INTREPID MAPS SECOND PORPHYRY TARGET AT CORRAL — 'Curly' Defined by QSP, Chalcopyrite, Molybdenite B-Veins in Arizona; IP Survey August, 5,000m Drill September (TSXV: INTR)
snippet: Intrepid Metals Corp. (TSXV: INTR) identified the Curly Porphyry Target through geological mapping and drill core review at its Corral Copper Project in Cochise County, Arizona, revealing porphyry-proximal alteration including QSP overprinting, stockwork veining, and quartz B-veins hosting chalcopyrite and molybdenite. Curly adds a second distinct porphyry target to the district-scale Corral property; an induced polarization survey in August will vector the September drill campaign, which has approximately 5,000 metres allocated to porphyry targets. Previous Corral drilling returned 216.5 metres of 0.71% copper from 29 metres depth, with high-grade intercepts to 5.94% Cu.

headline: BATTERY METALS RECOVERY HITS STOP-START EV DEMAND WALL — Li At Multi-Month Low as CATL, MinRes, Core Lithium All Add Supply
snippet: Mining.com's column tracks lithium carbonate testing CNY 154,000/T in mid-July — its lowest since March — as a wave of restarts compounds the supply side: CATL's Jianxiawo mine (100,000 t/yr capacity) secured its safety permit and resumed production on June 29, Mineral Resources restarted Bald Hill after an 18-month pause, and Core Lithium brought back Finniss. Lithium, cobalt, and nickel have all recovered substantially from their 2024–2025 lows, but the battery metals complex is now running into volatile EV demand that is compressing the spread between current prices and the incentive levels needed to justify major new mine builds.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH PRICE INDEX CLIMBS TO 271.9 — Heavy REE Supply Tight; Dysprosium and Terbium Hold at Elevated Levels as Domestic Market Leads Export Benchmarks
snippet: China's Rare Earth Price Index advanced to 271.9 with heavy rare earth supply remaining structurally tight, as dysprosium and terbium hold at historically elevated prices. The domestic Chinese benchmark is running ahead of export-facing equivalents — a divergence that points to domestic demand or policy factors rather than export curbs as the primary driver. Both elements are critical inputs for permanent magnets used in EV motors and wind turbines; sustained tightness in Chinese domestic pricing typically precedes pressure on downstream manufacturers in Japan, Europe, and North America, and is a direct leading indicator for Western rare earth explorers and producers.

headline: URANIUM Q2 REVIEW: TERM PRICES HOLD AS SPOT SOFTENS — Structural Deficit Intact; Wheeler River and New ISR Projects Advancing But New Supply Can't Fill the Gap Fast Enough
snippet: Investing News Network's Q2 2026 uranium review finds spot prices trending lower following Q1's multi-year highs while term contract prices remain firm — reflecting utilities' appetite to lock in long-term supply despite near-term spot softness. New supply timelines remain stretched: even Denison Mines' Wheeler River development and the newly producing ISR operations in Wyoming and Texas face years of ramp-up before making a material dent in the deficit. Uranium demand is set to expand significantly faster than mine output as reactor buildout accelerates globally, leaving the structural deficit that drove the cycle firmly intact through Q2 2026.
